title: Helmet Headset
tagline: A cheap Bluetooth neckband taken apart and rebuilt as a helmet headset
summary: Music, calls and navigation voice in your helmet for about ₹1,900–3,400 instead of a ₹5,000+ communicator, using a cheap Bluetooth neckband's own parts: its board, battery, both speakers and its mic. Its board, battery and buttons go in a pod stuck to the outside of the shell on the left with VHB tape (a universal size that fits most neckbands; a round play/call button and a dedicated volume rocker for gloves, sealed, USB-C at the back); the earbuds' own 10 mm speakers go in printed pucks in the liner's ear pockets; its mic goes on a bendable boom held on the helmet's fixed part, so a modular helmet's chin bar flips up over it. No holes in the helmet: the wires go in from below, in the grooves of a flexible cable channel stuck down the shell; besides the neckband, only small hardware bits. General purpose: the helmet's curve is a setting, and the neckband's parts are too, for a slimmer pod.
status: Designed and modelled (v1, checked in CAD, not printed or built yet). Designed first for a modular (flip-up) helmet. The pod is a universal size by default (room for a board up to 50 × 15 mm and a battery up to 50 × 28 × 7 mm), so most neckbands fit without measuring; enter your neckband's sizes for a slimmer pod.
see_sub: The pod on the left, behind the chin bar's pivot (the helmet is a plain stand-in); inside, the earbuds' speakers in the ear pockets and the neckband's mic on a boom.

gallery.caption: The pod on the left of a modular helmet (a white stand-in), behind the chin bar's pivot: stuck on with VHB tape, no holes

The pod at its universal size: 120 × 41 mm and 17.7 mm proud of the shell at its middle; a round play/call button and the volume rocker (raised + and −) in a screwed lid, the USB-C plug at its back end
Cut through the volume rocker: one rubber key over 2 switches; its solid middle rests on a small printed post, so pressing the top end gives louder and the bottom end quieter
The pod's bottom long side (the cable channel pulled away): the 2 cable notches right at the shell, facing down so rain runs past them; the channel's top end butts against the side and covers them

The cable channel: the cables leave the pod's bottom side (facing down, away from rain), a flexible TPU strip takes them straight down to the shell's lower edge, then in under the edge trim (no hole in the helmet)
Opened up: the lid, the TPU keypad (also the gasket), the switch board, the neckband's board and the battery
Inside (the stand-in cut open): the left earbud's speaker in its puck in the ear pocket, the neckband's mic on a boom held low on the fixed shell, reaching into the chin bar
The parts that go inside: a speaker puck holding the earbud's own 10 mm speaker, the boom mount and the mic cup
The cable channel turned over: a groove for each cable on its underside, thin flanges for the tape, its top end shaped to the pod's side

docs.label: README: what goes where, the neckband, the pod, wiring, build order

part_groups.label: The pod and its cable channel (outside)

pod_body.name: Pod body
pod_body.what: Holds the neckband's board, its battery and the switch board. Its underside is curved to the shell and stuck on with VHB tape; the USB-C hole at its back end, 2 cable notches in its bottom long side, right at the shell and facing down, lined up with the cable channel; 4 pillars for M2 heat-set inserts
pod_body.material: PETG or ASA, a light colour if you can. Open side down

pod_lid.name: Pod lid
pod_lid.what: Rolled edges, holes for the play/call button and the volume rocker, a ridge between them; 4 M2 × 6 countersunk screws

rocker_post.name: Rocker pivot post
rocker_post.what: A tiny 4 × 4 mm post glued to the switch board between the volume rocker's 2 switches: the rocker's solid middle rests on it and tips either way

keypad.name: Keypad
keypad.what: One TPU sheet with 2 keys: a round play/call button and a long volume rocker across the pod (raised + on its top end, − on its bottom end); its edge is the seam's gasket, squeezed 0.2 mm by the lid

usb_plug.name: USB-C plug
usb_plug.what: Seals the USB-C socket when you ride; pull it out by its tab (pointing up) to charge

speaker_puck.name: Speaker puck
speaker_puck.what: Holds the earbud's own 10 mm speaker (taken out of its shell) at the middle of the liner's ear pocket, with a small closed space behind it; the back is hollowed. Optional 40 mm helmet speakers fit it too (set the speaker size)

mic_cup.name: Mic cup
mic_cup.what: Holds the neckband's own mic on the end of the boom; a foam windscreen goes over it

boom_mount.name: Boom mount
boom_mount.what: A thin plate that slides between the shell and the liner (or sticks to the shell) low on the left, behind the chin bar; the boom pushes into its socket

headset_assembled.name: Pod, assembled
headset_assembled.what: The pod with its keypad, lid and plug

cable_channel.name: Cable channel
cable_channel.what: A flexible strip stuck to the shell: it runs straight down from the pod's bottom side (covering its cable notches) to the shell's lower edge. The 2 cables lie in the grooves on its underside, held flat against the shell, then go in under the edge trim. No hole in the helmet

params.name: shell_rl
params.label: Shell's radius along the pod (front to back)
params.help: Lay a ruler across the spot: radius = L × L / (8 × gap) + gap / 2.

params.name: shell_rw
params.label: Shell's radius across the pod (up and down)

params.name: run_l
params.label: Cable channel length
params.help: Along the shell, from the pod's bottom edge straight down to the shell's lower edge.

groups.label: Your neckband (the defaults fit most neckbands; enter yours for a slimmer pod)

params.name: nb_len
params.label: Board length (along the USB-C)
params.help: The defaults (board 50 × 15, battery 50 × 28 × 7) are a universal size: room for most neckbands, packed with foam. Measure your own for a slimmer pod.

params.name: nb_over
params.label: Tallest part on the board (not the USB-C)

params.name: usb_out
params.label: USB-C socket past the board's end

params.name: spk_d
params.label: Speaker diameter (the earbud's own driver)
params.help: The earbuds' own drivers: 10 mm on the Rockerz 255 Pro+. Optional 40 mm helmet speakers: 40 × 5.5.
